rationale: v4 wins on the two highest-weighted dimensions: actionability (+0.11 vs baseline) via a new Step 4 Pre-action Self-Check with 5 ordered yes/no gates plus an explicit 'modify X → re-run self-check' loop and a Step 6 halt that prevents skip-loops; and enforcement (+0.20) via a dedicated 'High-Risk Actions — 必经 User Gate' section enumerating 8 specific gated actions, Red Flags expanded from 7 to 12 with new codes for signals[] field completeness / stage.confidence missing / disabling user-managed skills / self-check bypass, and 4 additional rationalizations targeting the most likely evasion paths (fake standing-order, confidence-skip, list-available skip, GC excuse for user-edited fields). v3 was a very close runner-up (0.84) with the strongest integration layer of any variant: an ASCII end-to-end flow diagram, a full Manifest JSON Schema inline with field-level constraints (enable/disable disjoint, rationale covers enable∪disable, signals[] >= 1), a 4-command skillshare contract block with invariants, and an exp-sum signal JSON schema + flow-skill-research input/output contract. v3 only lost because its enforcement layer matches baseline+1-rationalization rather than v4's coded gates. v2 added valuable edge-case coverage (monorepo / submodule / corrupt manifest / opt-out / 7-day cooldown re-review / Q&A) that closes real ambiguity but lacks v3's contract schemas or v4's enforcement codes. v1 mostly compresses prose into tables for a small volume gain with no behavioral lift. Delta +0.08 exceeds the +0.05 improvement threshold. Recommended round-2 candidate: merge v4's High-Risk Actions + Pre-action Self-Check + RF-coded Red Flags with v3's Manifest Schema + skillshare command contract + signal JSON schema to push integration toward 0.90 while keeping enforcement at 0.92.
